facts.value: The November 10, 2026 agenda included a proposed moratorium on utility-scale BESS and associated infrastructure within Fairfax.
facts.supporting_summary: The draft would suspend acceptance for processing, consideration, approval and final action on applications for covered facilities and infrastructure, including site plans, rezonings and permits.

facts.value: The draft excludes ordinary residential batteries and certain small accessory systems, and distinguishes previously accepted complete applications from applications not yet accepted.
facts.supporting_summary: It would not invalidate a complete application lawfully submitted and accepted for processing before the effective date; a submitted application not yet accepted would be subject to the moratorium.

facts.value: The proposed term is 18 calendar months beginning on the ordinance's effective date, with possible early termination.
facts.supporting_summary: Early termination would be available if the council determines the study is complete and appropriate regulations are in place. The draft calls for effectiveness upon passage, approval and publication.

facts.value: The draft directs study and recommendations for permanent BESS regulation.
facts.supporting_summary: Study topics include fire and emergency response, setbacks, noise, environmental safeguards, zoning classifications, decommissioning and financial assurance.

facts.value: The council requested Planning and Zoning review and a recommendation on the 18-month proposal by a 4–1 vote.
facts.supporting_summary: Anderson, Daly, Wozniak and Wainwright voted aye; Mallie voted nay. The action was a referral, not adoption of the moratorium.

facts.value: The Planning and Zoning Commission voted unanimously to table the BESS moratorium.
facts.supporting_summary: The commission discussed the moratorium and approved a motion to table it. The same minutes separately discuss an Alliant BESS project.

facts.value: On October 27 the council set a November 10 public hearing; the amended November 10 agenda listed the hearing and proposal as items 7–8.
facts.locator: p. 2; see also nov10-agenda, p. 1, items 7–8
facts.supporting_summary: The hearing-setting motion carried with all present voting aye. The agenda does not document the November 10 outcome.

facts.topic: High-impact data-center moratorium and prohibition draft
facts.value: The separate draft attached to the November 10, 2026 agenda proposes a moratorium on municipal approvals for high-impact data centers and a prohibition in existing zoning districts.
facts.supporting_summary: The proposed moratorium has no fixed calendar term: it would remain until modified or repealed by a subsequent ordinance. Future authorization would require council legislation.

facts.topic: High-impact data-center moratorium and prohibition draft
facts.value: The draft uses several alternative criteria to classify high-impact data centers; 10 MW is one criterion, not the sole threshold.
facts.supporting_summary: Other criteria include dedicated utility infrastructure, industrial-scale cooling, large backup generation and utility-scale operational characteristics. Related phases and facilities may be aggregated.

facts.topic: High-impact data-center moratorium and prohibition draft
facts.value: The draft proposes infrastructure certifications and impact analyses for future consideration, and purports to apply on effectiveness to pending and future proposals to the fullest extent permitted by law.
facts.supporting_summary: Its requirements include utility certifications and economic, workforce, environmental and community analyses. The draft does not itself establish an actual effective date or a particular project's status.

facts.value: Agenda item 15 proposed a resolution to set a public hearing on a high-impact data-center prohibition; the unsigned resolution specifies December 8, 2026 at 6:00 p.m.
facts.locator: Sections 1–4, pp. 1–2; see also nov10-agenda, p. 3, item 15
facts.supporting_summary: The proposed hearing would be at Fairfax City Hall. The draft's preprinted November 10 passage line and unsigned signature lines do not establish that the resolution passed.

facts.value: The separate EU-3 draft would regulate data centers of every size and require rezoning into an EU-3 district.
facts.supporting_summary: The draft covers data centers and affiliated equipment, including BESS, and requires a major site plan and at least a 30-day evaluation period.

facts.value: The EU-3 draft proposes setbacks, noise and environmental controls, annual compliance testing, emergency-service support and an annual community contribution.
facts.supporting_summary: Examples include a 1,000-foot setback from residential zoning or public assembly, developer-funded testing and a proposed $1 million annual contribution during the facility's operational life.

facts.value: On October 13 the council adopted Resolution 2026-115 setting a hearing on proposed data-center zoning; the November 10 agenda listed an EU-3 hearing and proposal as items 9–10.
facts.locator: p. 3; see also nov10-agenda, p. 1, items 9–10
facts.supporting_summary: The hearing-setting resolution passed with all five council members voting aye. It was not adoption of the zoning ordinance.

facts.value: The EU-3 draft is labeled 2026-DC-01 and prints a July 15, 2026 first-reading date, but its reading and signature fields are blank.
facts.locator: p. 1 and signature page, PDF p. 7
facts.supporting_summary: The printed date alone does not establish that a reading occurred or that the ordinance was enacted.
